page_title: Let's build a URL shortener in Go - Final Part : Forwarding

summary.title: Let's build a URL shortener in Go - Final Part : Forwarding
summary.one_liner: You learn how to wire up the create-short-url and short-link redirect handlers in Go (with gin and Redis) so a shortened URL forwards to its original long URL.
keywords: how to redirect short link to long url
takeaways: Define two handlers: CreateShortUrl to generate and store a short link, and HandleShortUrlRedirect to look up and redirect.
CreateShortUrl parses the request body for the long URL and userId, generates a hash, and saves the mapping via the store layer.
The redirect handler reads the short URL from the path parameter, retrieves the original URL from the store, and issues an HTTP redirect.
The service runs on localhost:9808 and can be tested with any REST client by posting a URL and visiting the returned short link.
summary.summary: This final part of the series connects the components built earlier (short link generation and the Redis storage layer) into a working API. It creates a handler package with stubs for CreateShortUrl and HandleShortUrlRedirect, registers the endpoints /create-short-url and /:short-url in main.go, and then implements each handler step by step. The author then walks through testing: starting the server on port 9808, posting a create request, and visiting the returned short link to confirm it redirects. The page closes with links to the full GitHub repository and optional next steps such as Dockerizing, adding a SQL backup store, and building a front end.
